faq.q: What does it tell me when my JSON is invalid?
faq.a: It reports the error with a line and column number computed from the parse position, plus a context-aware hint — for example 'object keys must be double-quoted', 'check for trailing commas, single quotes, or unquoted keys', or 'input ended early — check for a missing closing } or ]'. Use 'Validate' for a quick check without reformatting.

faq.q: What formatting options and presets are there?
faq.a: Indent can be 2 spaces, 4 spaces or tab, with an optional 'Sort keys A→Z' (deep). Presets bundle these: Readable (2 spaces), Diff-friendly (2 spaces + sorted keys for clean diffs), Wide (4 spaces) and Tabs. You can Format/Beautify, Minify (showing bytes saved), or view a collapsible Tree View with per-node copyable JSON paths and a key/value search filter.

faq.q: What can it convert JSON into?
faq.a: CSV (flattened), YAML, a URL query string, and a TypeScript interface/type definition inferred from the data. There's also an Escape/Unescape tool for JSON string literals. The Stats panel reports total keys, max depth, a per-type count (string/number/boolean/null/object/array), and both pretty and minified byte sizes.

faq.q: Can it validate against a schema or diff two JSON documents?
faq.a: Yes. The schema validator takes simple 'key: type' lines (string, number, boolean, array, object) and reports which paths have the wrong type. The JSON Diff compares a second pasted JSON against the first and lists additions, removals and changed values by path. An 'Export all formats (ZIP)' button bundles JSON, minified JSON, CSV, YAML, TypeScript and query-string forms with a README. Everything runs locally and autosaves to your browser.
